I'm working out three analogous grid examples, each with two vertical reference lines and dots positioned relative to one line, then figuring out how to fill between the dot and the matching line.

For each variant I'm varying the number of dots (1, 2, then 3) and the line placements, making sure both lines stay the same length while checking that the mirrored fill pattern and frontier rows stay consistent with the rule structure I derived earlier.

Checking that dots only match one line each via row/column overlap, and confirming across variants that dots avoid overlapping with the second line's row range. I'm also verifying the count of distinct row versus column indices to distinguish vertical dot arrangements.

I realize the single-dot edge case would break this logic, since equal row/col counts default to the wrong axis. Sticking with multi-dot configurations avoids that ambiguity entirely.
